title: A rename carries over to canned jobs that hold the part
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a part, part A, for this test with 5 on hand.
  • Create a work order for this test, work order 1, with a line holding part A picked from stock.
  • Create a canned job for this test, canned job A, saved from that line, so it holds part A.
  • Use a new part number that no part and no Part Library entry has yet, and that does not contain part A's number.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.
custom_steps:
1. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  2. Click the part A row.
  3. Replace the Part Number with the new number.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Click Work Orders in the top bar.
  6. Open work order 1.
  7. Click New Line.
  8. Type canned job A's name in Title.
  9. Pick canned job A in the list.
  10. Click Save & Close.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Part A is listed.

Step 2:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A.

Step 3:

  • Part Number shows the new number.

Step 4:

  • The rename is saved and the window closes.

Step 5:

  • The Work Orders list opens.

Step 6:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 7:

  • The New Line window opens.

Step 8:

  • Canned job A is offered.

Step 9:

  • Canned job A is picked.

Step 10:

  • The canned job is added with its part under the new number, and no warning about parts left out appears.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog)

  • S13-R19: “A rename carries over to open work that holds this part, at every location: purchase order lines not yet fully received, part requests not yet received or returned, canned jobs, and returns that are not completed take the new number. A delivery that is not yet accepted is covered by its open purchase order lines. Receiving, ordering, applying a canned job and returning then find the renamed part.”
  • Story 13, context note: “Context note: S13-R19 matters because those records hold their own copy of the number and find the part by it later. Records already completed, such as received purchase order lines, completed returns and past work orders and invoices, keep the number they were written with. The Inventory list, Part History, Parts Velocity and today's Inventory Value show the new number. Inventory Value run for a date before the rename shows the number as it was on that date.”
  • Key Decisions: “A rename carries over to work that is still open. Open purchase order lines, open part requests, canned jobs and open returns follow the new number, so receiving and returning still find the part. Records already completed keep the number they were written with.”
